sanity_expectations: Bell-shaped in pH with a single interior maximum located between Ka1=6 and Ka2=8 (near pH ~7)
A approaches a residual plateau ~Aacid (~8) as pH -> low and ~Abase (~8) as pH -> high
A is finite, real, and positive everywhere on the grid; bounded roughly in [8, 100]
The bell shifts systematically with Temp (van't Hoff): with positive ionization enthalpies, warming lowers acidic-limb activity and raises basic-limb activity relative to the Temp=298 baseline
At Temp = Tref = 298 the curve reduces exactly to the parent (temperature term vanishes)
excitation_report: sigma=1.0 (~1% of peak activity ~100). auto_balance AND excitation_check were both invoked but ERROR OUT (SympifyError / tokenizer 'EOF in multi-line statement') because they re-parse the pipeline's stored expression string, which is malformed (net-unbalanced parentheses); they accept no expression argument, so the corrected RHS cannot be supplied to them. Excitation was therefore confirmed directly with analyze_expression (structure) + five check_substitution evaluations on the corrected, balanced RHS. Term visibility over pH in [3,11], Temp in [278,323]: (1) dominant Amax bell moves A from ~8 (limbs) to ~100 (peak near pH 7) => ~90 sigma. (2) Residual plateaus Aacid/Abase set the floor at ~8 => ~8 sigma. (3) NEW van't Hoff temperature term (E minus parent) is exactly 0 at Temp=Tref=298 (parent), so the Temp sweep is what exposes it: acidic limb pH=6 -> A=53.6 (Temp=298), 76.2 (Temp=278, delta +22.6), 39.9 (Temp=310, delta -13.7); basic limb pH=9 -> A=16.4 (Temp=298), 32.0 (Temp=323, delta +15.6). New-term peak effect ~14-23 sigma, strongest on the steep limbs (pH~6, pH~9) at the temperature extremes. All terms exceed 5 sigma.
role_corrections: A: output->output (confirmed dependent variable; LHS, explicitly solvable)

Temp: P->V (OVERRIDDEN: pipeline labeled fixed parameter, but it carries a range hint 278-323 and the new van't Hoff term dEnth*(1/Tref-1/Temp)/ln10R is only identifiable when Temp varies; at a single fixed Temp it collapses to a constant reparametrization of Ka1/Ka2, degenerate with the parent. Swept as 2nd independent axis)
Tref: P->P (confirmed fixed reference temperature, pinned 298)
dEnthAcid: P->P (confirmed; ionization-enthalpy coefficient to discover, fixed 40000 J/mol ~ 0.5 pKa shift over the sweep)
rationale: Structure (analyze_expression) confirms a static, explicitly-solvable algebraic relation A=(Amax+Aacid*E1+Abase*E2)/(1+E1+E2): no derivatives, no integral kernels, no ungoverned functions. This is a 3-state (acidic/active/basic) protonation model with electrostatic coupling (dpK, dpK2) between the two catalytic groups, giving the bell-shaped pH-activity profile. Hence equation_type=explicit, integrator=evaluate_explicit. Dependent variable A; the only role override is Temp (parameter->independent variable): the evolution step's NEW content is the van't Hoff temperature dependence of the effective pKa midpoints, which is unidentifiable at a single temperature (it would merely re-label Ka1/Ka2). The pipeline itself hints this by giving Temp a range (278-323) while pinning Tref=298 and ln10R=19.14. So the dataset sweeps both pH (3-11, 40 pts) and Temp (278-323, 11 pts) => 440 points. Parameter magnitudes are physiological: pKa1=6, pKa2=8, Hill coeffs 1, small residual activities (8) vs peak (100), coupling shifts 0.6, and ionization enthalpies 40 kJ/mol (within the -40000..60000 hint) which produce ~+/-0.5 pKa-unit shifts across the Temp sweep. IMPORTANT INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE: auto_balance and excitation_check both fail to sympify because they load the pipeline's stored expression string, which is malformed (unbalanced parentheses -> tokenizer 'EOF in multi-line statement') and cannot be overridden via an argument. I reconstructed the mathematically-identical, balanced RHS (verified by analyze_expression returning the full symbol set + explicit solvability, and by check_substitution returning finite/real values with zero residual free symbols at five grid points) and quantified excitation manually via check_substitution deltas against the parent (Temp=Tref) baseline. All additive terms, including the new temperature term (~14-23 sigma), exceed 5 sigma at sigma=1.0. rhs_for_integrator is the corrected, balanced expression so downstream data generation is not blocked by the malformed source string.
